case.goal: Get Chakan’s October GSTR-1 right, tie it to the books and check the 3B credit against GSTR-2B before the tax is paid.
case.where: Firm office, Prabhat Road · Wednesday 4 November to Monday 16 November 2026

messages: Tamhini’s October returns are yours. Sort Pallavi’s sales file into Chakan’s GSTR-1 and tie it to the books by Friday; their plant shuts for Diwali after that, and R1 is due on the 11th.
2B comes on the 14th. Then check her 3B working against it and draft the note to Mahesh; I file the 3B by the 20th.

tasks.title: Sort October’s sales invoices
tasks.prompt: Pallavi’s October folder holds these 12 invoices. For each, pick the GSTR-1 it goes in: Chakan’s for October or November, Hosur’s, or none. Then say where in Chakan’s October return. Our registrations sheet, the gate register and her mail are under Other papers. Your calls go to Neethu when you move on.

lockOnLeave.note: You can’t change them after this.
lockOnLeave.done: Handed to Neethu. You can read your calls but not change them.

hints: Read the GSTIN printed at the top of each invoice first: whose GSTIN it is decides whose GSTR-1 it goes in, whoever the buyer is.
Check the month-end invoices against the gate register: an invoice made before or when the truck leaves keeps its own month. A cancelled number still counts in Table 13.

items.label: Invoice 1 · Ashvaratha Motors
items.note: Invoice 1: Chakan to Ashvaratha’s plant at Chakan, both in Maharashtra, so CGST and SGST. B2B in Chakan’s GSTR-1, ₹66,21,600 taxable. The plain case; most of the month looks like this.

items.label: Invoice 2 · Lothal Motors
items.note: Invoice 2: the goods go to Sanand in Gujarat. The place of supply is outside Maharashtra, so the tax is IGST, ₹9,32,580, and it is B2B in Chakan’s GSTR-1.

items.label: Invoice 3 · Naik Auto Spares
items.note: Invoice 3: stamped cancelled the day it was made, and the IRN cancelled with it. It goes in no B2B table, but the number was used, so Table 13 counts it under cancelled for the TD/TR series.

items.label: Invoice 4 · Tamhini, Hosur depot
items.note: Invoice 4: Chakan to Tamhini’s own Hosur depot. Two registrations of one PAN are distinct persons, so this transfer is a supply: B2B in Chakan’s GSTR-1, Hosur’s GSTIN as the buyer, IGST ₹8,96,940. Hosur takes the credit.

items.label: Invoice 5 · Ponni Motors
items.note: Invoice 5: look at the top. The seller is 33ZHDCT5940H1ZB, the Hosur depot, not Chakan. Hosur files its own GSTR-1 in Tamil Nadu, so this one stays out of Chakan’s return, whatever the sales register says.

items.label: Invoice 6 · Bilal Ferrous Traders
items.note: Invoice 6: scrap is a sale like any other. Bilal’s truck takes it to Bhosari, Pune, so CGST and SGST, ₹95,287.50 each, and B2B. Its HSN, 7204 41, gets its own line in the HSN summary, Table 12.

items.label: Invoice 7 · Wardha Road Auto
items.note: Invoice 7: Nagpur is a long way from Chakan, but it is in Maharashtra. Same State, so CGST and SGST and Chakan’s B2B table. Distance never decides the tax; the State of the place of supply does.

items.label: Invoice 8 · Kosli Driveline
items.note: Invoice 8: Manesar is in Haryana, so IGST, ₹9,15,246, B2B in Chakan’s GSTR-1.

items.label: Invoice 9 · Golconda Motor Spares
items.note: Invoice 9: Secunderabad is in Telangana, so IGST, ₹2,23,884. Golconda is a dealer with a GSTIN, which makes it B2B, not B2C. B2C is only for buyers with no registration.

items.label: Invoice 10 · Vaigai Axle Systems
items.note: Invoice 10: Hosur’s GSTIN again, 33ZHDCT5940H1ZB, and a buyer in Tamil Nadu, so CGST and SGST charged by Hosur. It belongs in Hosur’s GSTR-1. Pallavi’s register mixes both because the books are one company.

items.label: Invoice 11 · Vayuvega Two Wheelers
items.note: Invoice 11: dated 31 October; the truck came on 2 November. An invoice may be issued before the goods move, and one issued on time fixes the month by its date. October’s GSTR-1, B2B, CGST and SGST. Tell Pallavi to keep it in October.

items.label: Invoice 12 · Kshitij Driveline
items.note: Invoice 12: the shafts were packed on 31 October, but the invoice is dated 2 November, the day the truck left. Issued on time, so its date decides: November’s GSTR-1. It is in November’s books too.

notes.r1.ig: Pallavi took IGST from the sales register alone and missed the transfers’ ₹29,81,700. Chakan supplied those goods, so the tax is Chakan’s.
notes.r1.cg: Chakan’s CGST only. The ₹16,20,540 of CGST on Hosur’s bills is the Hosur GSTIN’s tax and goes in Hosur’s own 3B.
notes.r3.ig: Kolak missed KP/26-27/1187 in its GSTR-1 and added it through GSTR-1A on 13 November. That lands in November’s 2B, so the ₹25,200 is claimed in November’s 3B.

notes.r5.ig: The registers less the two gaps equal 2B under every head, so nothing is left unexplained.
notes.r6.ig: No head’s credit is more than its tax, so each head pays its own and nothing crosses over. Total cash ₹47,58,356.

tasks.title: Draft the note to Mahesh
tasks.prompt: Mahesh needs one mail from us: what changed in October’s returns and what his team does next. Pick the right line for each point.
hints: Credit follows GSTR-2B. A bill uploaded late is claimed in the month 2B shows it; a bill 2B does not show gets no credit, though the purchase stands. The GSTIN that issues an invoice reports it.

options.text: Alandi Paper Products: its GSTIN has been cancelled since 15 September, and its October bills (GST ₹11,500) are not in GSTR-2B. We have kept this credit out of October’s 3B; please hold back that GST from Alandi’s payments.
options.why: The credit waits for 2B, and 2B will not show it while the registration stays cancelled. The supplier answers for the GST it charged.

options.text: Alandi Paper Products: its GSTIN has been cancelled since 15 September, but the boxes came in and the bills are genuine, so we have claimed the ₹11,500 in October’s 3B. We will check its status again next month.
options.why: Genuine bills are not enough. Alandi’s October bills are not in 2B, so there is no credit to claim.

options.text: Alandi Paper Products: its GSTIN has been cancelled since 15 September, so its October bills are void. Please reverse the ₹2,30,000 of purchases from your books, send the boxes back to Alandi and stop its payments.
options.why: The purchase stands: the boxes came and went into packing. Only the ₹11,500 of GST credit is in question.

options.text: Kolak Polypack: bill KP/26-27/1187 of 29 October (IGST ₹25,200) is not in October’s 2B, so this credit is lost for good. Please reverse it in your books and ask Kolak to refund the tax.
options.why: Not lost. Kolak added the bill through GSTR-1A, and it comes in November’s 2B.

options.text: Kolak Polypack: bill KP/26-27/1187 of 29 October (IGST ₹25,200) was added through Kolak’s GSTR-1A on 13 November, after the cut-off, so it comes in November’s 2B. We will claim it in November’s 3B.
options.why: A late upload only moves the credit to the month whose 2B shows the bill.

options.text: Kolak Polypack: bill KP/26-27/1187 of 29 October (IGST ₹25,200) already shows in GSTR-2A through Kolak’s GSTR-1A of 13 November, so we have claimed it in October’s 3B with Kolak’s other bills.
options.why: The 3B credit follows 2B, not 2A. This bill comes in November’s 2B, so it is claimed in November’s 3B.

options.text: From November, please keep stock transfers out of the sales data. They are only movements between your own units, so they go in neither GSTR-1, and Hosur’s invoices can stay in Chakan’s GSTR-1.
options.why: Two registrations of one PAN are distinct persons, so a transfer between them is a supply that Chakan reports.

options.text: From November, please send the stock transfer register with the sales register. Transfers to Hosur go only in the Tamil Nadu GSTR-1, as Hosur receives the goods, and Hosur’s invoices go there too.
options.why: The supplier reports, not the receiver. Chakan issues the transfer invoices, so they go in Chakan’s GSTR-1; Hosur sees them in its 2B.

options.text: From November, please send the stock transfer register with the sales register. Transfers to Hosur go in Chakan’s GSTR-1 as B2B supplies with IGST, and Hosur’s own invoices go in the Tamil Nadu GSTR-1.
options.why: Each GSTIN reports what it issued: Chakan the transfer invoices, Hosur its bills to Ponni and Vaigai.

freeText.label: Your own line for the mail

wrap.text: Pallavi took two shortcuts this month: she treated the sales register as Chakan’s GSTR-1 and the purchase register as the 3B credit. November’s returns start with the same two checks. Mahesh gets your note now and my 3B figures this afternoon.

wrapPartial.text: Chakan’s GSTR-1 holds what Chakan’s GSTIN issued in October, transfers to Hosur included. The 3B takes only the credit GSTR-2B shows. I file the 3B only when every head ties to the rupee.

wrapRetry.text: Read the GSTIN at the top of each invoice and the date it was issued: together they tell you whose return and which month. Then put the purchase register next to 2B, supplier by supplier, before you touch the 3B.

passNeeds.note: You need 9 of the 12 invoice calls right to pass; the right GSTR-1 with the wrong table counts half.

model.intro: Chakan’s GSTR-1 reports one GSTIN’s supplies, not the company’s sales register: Hosur’s invoices go to Hosur’s GSTR-1, the stock transfers come in and the 2 November invoice waits. In the 3B the credit follows GSTR-2B, so Kolak’s bill moves to November and Alandi’s bills stay out.

blocks.text: If a GSTR-1 mistake turns up after filing, put it right in GSTR-1A before the 3B is filed, so the 3B follows a correct GSTR-1.

principles: GSTR-1 is filed per GSTIN: report what that registration supplied, transfers to your other GSTINs included.
For goods, an invoice issued on time (before or when the goods leave) fixes the month by its date; a late invoice takes the day they left.
3B credit stops at what GSTR-2B shows, and every gap from the books gets a reason and someone to act on it.

interview.q: What’s the difference between GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B?
interview.checking: Whether you know which return carries the detail and which carries the tax.
outline: GSTR-1 lists outward supplies, invoice by invoice for B2B, due by the 11th for monthly filers.
GSTR-3B is the summary: tax on supplies, credit from GSTR-2B, then the cash, by the 20th.
Its tax is auto-filled from GSTR-1[[, so in the simulation I tied GSTR-1 to the books first{turn|}]].

interview.q: The books show more input credit than GSTR-2B. What goes in the 3B?
interview.checking: Whether you know GSTR-2B caps the credit, and can give a reason for every bill it leaves out.
outline: Only what GSTR-2B shows, and only if eligible; the purchase register alone does not give the credit.
In the simulation one bill came through GSTR-1A after the cut-off, so it waits for November.
Another supplier’s GSTIN was cancelled, so 2B did not show its bills[[; I kept that credit out{gone|}{gone2|}]].
